technologies.how: Pointers, explicit allocation, atomics, structs, and stable C ABIs.
technologies.name: C
technologies.what: Provides direct memory and hardware control with a minimal runtime.
technologies.when: Use when deterministic layout, ABI control, or near-zero runtime overhead is mandatory.
technologies.where: Firmware, kernels, embedded loops, lock-free primitives, and portable system libraries.
technologies.why: It is the universal systems interoperability layer and maps closely to machine execution.

technologies.how: RAII, templates, ranges, atomics, custom allocators, and vectorized numerical kernels.
technologies.name: C++
technologies.what: Combines low-level control with zero-cost abstractions and mature numerical libraries.
technologies.when: Use when performance and complex abstractions must coexist in one native binary.
technologies.where: Engines, inference runtimes, cache systems, geometry, simulation, and latency-sensitive services.
technologies.why: It provides deterministic ownership patterns, templates, SIMD access, and unmatched systems-library depth.

technologies.how: Ownership, lifetimes, enums, traits, Result types, channels, and zero-cost abstractions.
technologies.name: Rust
technologies.what: Builds native systems with compile-time ownership, thread safety, and no garbage collector.
technologies.when: Use when native performance and strong memory/concurrency guarantees are both non-negotiable.
technologies.where: Evidence engines, action governors, cryptographic tooling, network services, and safe concurrency.
technologies.why: The borrow checker eliminates broad classes of memory corruption and data races before execution.

technologies.how: Comptime, explicit allocators, error unions, slices, and C ABI integration.
technologies.name: Zig
technologies.what: Builds explicit, portable native software with compile-time metaprogramming and excellent C interop.
technologies.when: Use when cross-target delivery, allocator control, or C integration dominates.
technologies.where: Portable CLIs, allocators, cross-compilation, embedded tools, and small runtime components.
technologies.why: It provides explicit failure paths, no hidden allocation, and first-class cross-compilation.

technologies.how: Explicit allocators, context values, arrays, structs, procedures, and SIMD-friendly layouts.
technologies.name: Odin
technologies.what: Prioritizes data-oriented native programming with explicit memory contexts and low hidden complexity.
technologies.when: Use when data layout, allocator visibility, and predictable control flow are central.
technologies.where: Game engines, physics, visualization, and deterministic real-time loops.
technologies.why: It presents a simpler C-like systems model with built-in data-oriented facilities.

technologies.how: Tables, metatables, lexical environments, pcall, and host-provided capability injection.
technologies.name: Lua
technologies.what: Provides a tiny, portable embeddable scripting runtime for host-controlled extension.
technologies.when: Use when untrusted or third-party logic must run under an explicit capability table.
technologies.where: Game engines, plugin hosts, config loaders, agent tool sandboxes, and embedded automation.
technologies.why: Its small core and first-class environments make capability isolation practical without a heavyweight runtime.
